name: Average Teaching Dimension of the Universal Class
proof: The universal class $\mathcal U_n=\{u_i:i\in[n]\}$ on domain $2^{[n]}$ has $u_i(A)=1$ exactly when $i\in A$. At $n=1$ it contains one concept, which is uniquely identified by the empty sample, so every individual minimum teaching-set size is zero. For $n\ge2$, the labeled instance $(\{i\},1)$ uniquely identifies $u_i$, while the empty sample identifies no target in a class with at least two concepts. Thus every individual minimum teaching-set size is one. Averaging these individual minimum teaching-set sizes gives average teaching dimension.
details: For every n>=1. The singleton endpoint is zero; the earlier unqualified constant-one value omitted this case.
